title: Algebraic Symmetry Test of a Rational Function
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Algebraically determine whether the function h(x) = \frac{x^3}{x^2 + 4} is even, odd, or neither, and describe the geometric symmetry of its graph.
hints: Compute h(-x) by substituting -x for every occurrence of x in the formula.
Simplify odd and even powers of (-x).
Compare the simplified expression for h(-x) with h(x) and with -h(x).
finalAnswer: Odd function; symmetric with respect to the origin

steps.title: Evaluate h(-x)
steps.explanation: Substitute -x into the function definition to test how it responds to reflection across the y-axis.
steps.why: Testing function parity requires evaluating the algebraic definition at the opposite input -x.

steps.title: Simplify Exponent Powers
steps.explanation: The numerator has an odd exponent 3, so (-x)^3 = -x^3. The denominator has an even exponent 2, so (-x)^2 = x^2.
steps.why: Odd powers preserve negation, while even powers eliminate negation.

steps.title: Relate to Original Function
steps.explanation: Factoring the minus sign out of the fraction demonstrates that h(-x) = -h(x) for all real x.
steps.why: By definition, any function satisfying h(-x) = -h(x) on a symmetric domain is an odd function.

steps.title: State Geometric Symmetry
steps.explanation: The graph of an odd function has 180-degree rotational symmetry about the origin (0, 0).
steps.why: Every point (x, y) on the graph of an odd function has a corresponding reflected point (-x, -y) on the graph.
